options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: Every child recovers immediately without support.

options.label: C

groups.heading: Advanced: Distinguish qualifications and implications
groups.instruction: Listen to the episode and choose the best answer to each question. Questions follow the recording.
groups.answerInstruction: Choose ONE answer: A, B or C.

questions.prompt: What connection does Asma ask Fergal to consider?

options.label: A
options.text: Whether all journalists had the same childhood as him.

options.label: B
options.text: Why reporting had prevented him from remembering his childhood.

options.label: C
options.text: How his childhood experiences influenced his reporting on children.

questions.prompt: What distinction is made between vigilance and hypervigilance?

options.label: A
options.text: The latter can involve an excessive level of alertness and anxiety.

options.label: B
options.text: The latter means paying less attention to danger.

options.label: C
options.text: The two words refer to different physical locations.

questions.prompt: What does the researchers' agreement establish in the discussion?

options.label: A
options.text: Agreement that every aspect of their research is settled.

options.label: B
options.text: Agreement on one condition for recovery despite disagreements on other matters.

options.label: C
options.text: Agreement that recovery is independent of a child's current circumstances.

questions.prompt: Which interpretation of the proposed approach does Fergal explicitly rule out?

options.label: A
options.text: Approaching ordinary activities gradually.

options.label: B
options.text: Making children face death and massacre again.

options.label: C
options.text: Recognising that sleeping alone may be difficult.

questions.prompt: Why does Fergal compare the situation with an ordinary childhood nightmare?

options.label: A
options.text: To show that an apparently simple bedtime task can still be very difficult.

options.label: B
options.text: To claim that every nightmare is a result of war.

options.label: C
options.text: To suggest that war trauma is no more serious than a dream.

questions.prompt: Why is the expression "given a chance" important to Fergal's final observation?

options.label: A
options.text: It means resilience can be measured by counting dreams.

options.label: B
options.text: It removes the need to address continuing danger.

options.label: C
options.text: It qualifies his optimism by recognising that recovery needs an opportunity.
